## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

We need build new game, likely replace existing Molt. User request pong-like game: 2D, player moves bar up/down to bounce ball, top/bottom walls bounce, objective first to 5 points vs another player or AI enemy. Need build complete playable game. Need use existing blank repo? It's a huge previous game. We can replace. Need infer expected deliverable includes perhaps desktop/mobile. Must run and screenshot with Playwright. Need inspect package? None. Static. Need build likely HTML/CSS/JS Canvas. Need create polished game. Key requirements:
- 2D game
- player bar moves up and down (vertical paddle? Actually "move up and down a white bar to made a ball bounce"; "Uper and lower area bounce ball"; points when ball passes back of other player). This sounds like Pong rotated 90°: vertical court? Let's parse carefully: "player move up and down a withe bar to made a ball bounce. Uper and lower area bounce ball, objetive is to made 5 poimts vs another player. The poimts are made when the ball pass the back of the otjer player, or the IA enemy"

They mention move up/down white bar, upper/lower area bounce ball, pass back of other player. This is likely horizontal court where two paddles move vertically at left and right, ball bounces off top and bottom. "Upper and lower area bounce ball" means top/bottom walls bounce. "pass the back of the other player" means ball goes behind paddle at left/right. So Pong with vertical paddles, horizontal ball. Player's paddle on left, moves up and down; AI on right, moves up/down. Score when ball passes a paddle. First to 5. Good.

Need create high-quality polished game. Need perhaps title screen, local 2P vs CPU, sound, pause, reset, responsive, touch. Need implement with Canvas. Need perhaps choose visual style. Existing uses watercolor; we can replace completely. Need maybe preserve README? User expects game build. We can overwrite index, css, js. Keep asset free. Aim for excellent game: "NEON RALLY" or "Top Spin"? White bar requirement—white bar. Let's make stylish retro-futurist "VERTEX" or "RALLY/5" with dark blue/teal, court grid, glowing ball and white paddles. Could make an elegant minimalist "CROSSCOURT" or "NEON PONG". Need avoid generic maybe polished.

We should use clear game states: title menu with mode selection CPU (3 difficulties) or 2P local. Start button. First to 5. Side labels. Countdown. Score display. Win screen. Pause. Controls. On-screen touch drag. Keyboard W/S or arrow up/down for left; 2P uses W/S and Up/Down. For CPU mode, player left, CPU right. Serve starts toward random side. Ball bouncing top/bottom. Score when crossing beyond paddle x. Maybe spin based on paddle movement. Add particles, trails, screen shake, hit flashes, rally count, slow-mo? Keep compelling.

Need clarify "pass the back" maybe ball must pass behind paddle to score. We'll score if ball crosses paddle plane without collision; even if ball outside court vertical. Since top/bottom bounce, always within unless paddle collision only. Use score when ball x < -ball radius on left or > width+radius right. That is "back of player".

Need figure what app harness expects. Likely starts static server on 3002, capture script. Need use screenshot function. Check .omgithub checkpoint maybe captures instructions.

This repository bundles the baseline skills installed by [Worker
Agents](https://github.com/agents-dev/workerAgents).

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D paddle duel: player controls a white bar vertically, ball bounces off top/bottom walls, first to 5 points wins, with CPU or local 2-player modes.
- Replace the existing Molt game with a polished “Night Rally” game.

## Requirements
- Player moves up/down to bounce the ball; top and bottom walls bounce it.
- Points are scored when the ball passes behind the opponent’s paddle.
- First to 5 points wins.
- Support both CPU opponent and local 2-player.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks and inspect only the latest one.

## Decisions
- Game title: **Night Rally**, subtitle/tagline “First to five.”
- Visual style: dark teal night court, white glowing paddles, mint (player) and coral (CPU/P2) accents, serif italic title mixed with condensed sans headline.
- Rotated Pong layout: left/right vertical paddles, horizontal ball, top/bottom walls.
- CPU difficulties: CALM, SHARP, RUTHLESS with distinct speed, reaction, error, anticipation, and mistake rates.
- Controls: WASD or arrows for solo; P1 `W/S`, P2 `↑/↓` locally; drag on touch; any side in solo, corresponding half in local.
- Added start menu, pause modal, match results, score pips, rally counter, procedural Web Audio SFX, mute persistence, responsive layout, and debug handle `window.__nightRally`.
- Changed footer text from “WIN BY ONE” to “NO MERCY” because the game is strictly first to 5.
- Fixed result grammar: “YOU TAKE IT.” vs “P1/P2/CPU TAKES IT.”

## Work State
### Completed
- Replaced `index.html` with the Night Rally interface.
- Replaced `css/style.css` with full responsive styling.
- Replaced `js/audio.js` with procedural sound effects.
- Created `js/rally.js` with game loop, physics, CPU AI, scoring, overlays, touch/keyboard input, rendering, particles, menu attract mode, debug hooks.
- Desktop and mobile screenshots show playable menu, gameplay, score announcement, pause, and result screens.
- CPU balance tested with a simulated delayed human paddle:
  - CALM: player 5–2, ~39s
  - SHARP: player 5–3, ~54s
  - RUTHLESS: CPU 5–0, ~66s
- Fixed score pips visibility, safe-area-aware court layout, mobile footer/rule strip, and aria-hidden state handling.

### Active
- Recently added mobile menu rule strip using `<span>`s in `.aside-copy`; needs visual verification after reload.
- Need final visual checks at desktop and mobile, plus 2-player/local mode and pointer/touch control tests.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Reload and screenshot mobile menu (`390x844`) to verify the new bottom rule strip and footer.
2. Resize to `1440x900`, screenshot menu and gameplay; verify desktop aside panel no longer collides awkwardly with the right paddle.
3. Test local 2P: select LOCAL, start, confirm right paddle responds to `↑/↓` (or drag right half) and labels switch to P1/P2.
4. Test mouse/touch drag: `pointerdown` on canvas + move changes paddle position.
5. Check browser console for errors; verify no runtime issues after recent CSS/HTML edits.
6. Optionally run a final playthrough/result screenshot and clean up stale screenshots.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: game UI, menu, HUD, pause/end overlays.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/css/style.css`: all visual styling and responsive rules.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: latest QA screenshots (`menu-mobile2.jpg`, `game-mobile2.jpg`, etc.).
